key_insight: The paper shows that encoder--decoder operator learning can be analyzed in a resolution-independent way by proving that the induced kernels converge to a limiting kernel, so error bounds separate encoding effects from optimization effects.
engineering_relevance: This gives practitioners a principled way to compare and design discretization-dependent learning systems such as neural operators, PDE surrogates, and other function-to-function models across changing input/output resolutions.
method: Builds operator-valued kernels from matrix-valued kernels on encoded spaces and proves the associated RKHSs are isometrically isomorphic.
Establishes operator-norm convergence of induced integral operators to a limiting kernel as resolution increases.
Derives upper and lower learning-rate/error bounds for regularized SGD and extends the analysis to encoder--decoder networks via limiting NTKs.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical upper and lower error bounds, plus polynomial parameter and sample complexity guarantees when encoding errors decay algebraically.
watch_item: The framework is asymptotic and depends on encoding errors decaying with resolution, so finite-resolution performance and implementation details may still vary substantially.
paper_title: Resolution-Independent Analysis of Encoder--Decoder Operator Learning via Limiting Kernels
